question: Heinrich XIII Prinz Reuss has been held in pre-trial detention since December 2022. A press report from September 2026 claims he has been held in isolation and subjected to degrading physical searches after visits.

1 Already back in May 2024, his defence counsel had objected to the use of partition screens during meetings with their client and to the appointment of a reading judge to monitor correspondence with the defence counsel.2 The case raises fundamental questions about dignified, proportionate pre-trial detention and effective defence.
The standards that should apply are provided for in Recommendation (EU) 2023/681 and Directive 2013/48/EU. 1.

On the basis of the standards set out in Recommendation (EU) 2023/681, how does the Commission assess the reported cases of solitary confinement and body searches in cases of long-term pre-trial detention?

Under what conditions are partitions in meetings with the defence counsel and the monitoring of correspondence with the defence counsel by a reading judge compatible with Articles 3 and 4 of Directive 2013/48/EU?

What specific steps can the Commission take, within the limits of its competences vis-àvis Germany, to investigate these allegations regarding the application of its detention standards and possible breaches of the rights of defence under EU law?
